chapter: Learning the trade in Los Angeles
title: Growling like Cootie, 'Fiesta in Blue', and other idols
summary: He discusses his growl playing, his surprising Cootie-style solo on 'Fiesta in Blue' with Basie, and his favorites Joe Smith, Armstrong and Cootie.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Did you do, were you doing sort of growl trumpet like Cootie then?
Yes, but I, I wasn't doing it, I couldn't do it like, I never could do it like Cootie.
Now certain things Cootie used to play that he didn't growl on. Like 'Ring them Bells'.
Yes. Well he was a ( ?).
But I used to play some things he did.
Well what was that thing you did years later when you did play Cootie style? What was that?
'Old Man River'?
No, there was a thing you played while with Basie.....
Oh, 'Fiesta in Blue'.
Yes. Well I mean there you got — I mean people didn't know you could do it when you did that.
Yes, but you see that record wasn't made for me, that arrangement. Mundy made it.
Jimmy Mundy?
Yes, yes. He brought it to

Basie, gave it to all four trumpet players before I got it. He started on this end and I happened to be sitting on this end. So Ed Lewis tried it, Al Killian tried it and I don't think it was Harry, somebody else was in there. Anyway, when it got to me, I was the only one that kind of made it like they wanted it. So they, they......
Well that you hadn't done on Basie's records, I mean....
I hadn't before, no.
That was a surprise to people that you could sound so much like Cootie.
Cootie made it too. He made 'Fiesta in Blue'.
Did he?
Yes. And another thing that Cootie and I made was 'West End Blues'. I think Cootie made 'West End Blues'?
Yes he did with a small band.
Yes I think he did. Or maybe I'm confusing it with ....
When did you make 'West End Blues'?
I made it in Europe, Panassie. Yes, for Panassie. But I know he made 'Fiesta in Blue'.
I think he made it with Benny wasn't it?
Could be.
I think it was. I know he didn't make it with Duke.
No, no.
So Cootie also, although I had other people that I liked. I said I liked (King) Porter.* I liked Joe Smith.
Oh yes.
I liked Joe Smith.
Yes, well I was going to say, the muted thing that, the muted thing really came later when you got with Basie.
Right.
That wasn't, at this time that wasn't your forte really?
No, Basie always wanted me to do that.
